Arithmetic R43/R32 N 0.70/0.83=0.84, S 0.22/0.39=0.56 agrees. N-S 5.1" separation makes deblending negligible: agree.

Did not re-run the cube extraction. Concerns found on reading: (i) HCN 4-3 (X1df1, native 0.87x0.69") and HCO+ 4-3 (X858, native 0.39x0.35") are from different projects/configurations, so uv coverage and missing-flux differ; channel-wise convolution to a common beam equalises beam size, not the short-spacing sensitivity. The HCN/HCO+ ratio at S (extended, weak) is the most exposed. (ii) S HCN 4-3 centroid is 2718 vs HCO+ 2743 km/s at 1.0" (25 km/s, converges to 2760/2760 only at 2.5"), while HCN FWHM is 120 vs 192 km/s: the Gaussian fit to a ~18 sigma, narrower, shifted line indicates a blend/asymmetry, not a clean ratio; an integral over a common velocity window was requested ('matched velocity windows') but a Gaussian-fit moment-0 was used. (iii) Errors are statistical only (fit error x1.3); classification probabilities use 'Gaussian 0.1' for the extrapolation, ad hoc and without the ~10-15% per-project flux-scale error on a ratio built from two projects. (iv) The core 4-3 value for N (0.88) is an extrapolation by assuming R43/R32 constant to 56 pc; for S the measured R43/R32 itself falls toward small beams (0.66->0.56), so the S core 4-3 is probably below 0.26 and N is not shown to be flat below 188 pc. (v) The 1-0 values (0.60-0.65) cited in the verdict entry are not traced to a script/output in the summary.

fixes.what: Test uv-matching of the 4-3 ratio: re-make both 4-3 cubes with a common uv range (and common taper) or compare the ratio after restricting both to the shared baseline range (e.g. >~30 m to the shortest of the two projects' longest-baseline limits) and check recovered flux vs MRS of each execution.
fixes.why: Different projects/configs for HCN and HCO+ can bias the ratio, especially at extended S; S 4-3=0.22 is the key 'false negative' claim.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Compare uv-coverage plots/MRS from the archive headers, apply uvtaper/uvrange in imaging or compute visibilities-based amplitude ratio in annuli; report the ratio with and without this restriction.

fixes.what: Replace the Gaussian-fit moment-0 by integration over one fixed common velocity window (e.g. centred on the CO/HCO+ systemic velocity of each nucleus, same width for both lines) and show the HCN and HCO+ 4-3 spectra at S and N (overlay in velocity) at 1.0" and 1.9". Explain the 25 km/s centroid and 120 vs 192 km/s width mismatch at S.
fixes.why: Brief required matched velocity windows; the S HCN line looks narrower/shifted, so the Gaussian area may under-represent HCN and push the ratio low.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Use moment-0 on a common window with noise from line-free channels, check blends (HCN v2=1, H13CN/other lines in window), and quote ratio from integrated rather than fitted flux.

fixes.what: Redo the error budget: add per-project flux-scale (~10% each, 4-3 from two projects => ~14% on the ratio; 3-2 likewise if two EBs/projects) and pointing/astrometric uncertainty of the fixed N/S position; then recompute the N and S classification probabilities by Monte Carlo (state input distributions) instead of ad hoc 'Gaussian 0.1'. Also give the ratio at the peak position of each line vs the fixed position.
fixes.why: With ~0.12 systematic on N's 0.88, P(SB<=1.03) is likely ~0.85-0.9 and P(>=1.1) is not <0.03; also the S 'below AGN' result is robust but should be quantified.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Monte Carlo with stat+syst, report the posterior probability and the dependence on the extrapolation model (flat R43/R32 vs RADEX range).

fixes.what: Make the N statement unambiguous: given P~0.9 that N core is <=1.03 yet 0.88-1.0 sits at the top of the SB range and 2x the SB median, state explicitly that at the N core the 4-3 diagnostic is not discriminating (per task instructions) while at >=188 pc N is clearly SB-like (0.57-0.70), instead of 'only weakly discriminating'. Do not call N a 'partial false positive' without noting that 3-2 1.05 at 56 pc is also inside literature ULIRG medians.
fixes.why: Wording currently mixes 'weakly discriminating', 'not AGN-like' and 'partial false positive'.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: One table: scale, J, ratio+-(stat,syst), Izumi class interval, probability SB/AGN.

fixes.what: Show whether R43/R32 for N is really flat toward smaller beams: use 3-2 at 0.3-0.75" with the extrapolation uncertainty from the observed S trend (0.66->0.56), and give N core 4-3 as a range with that slope; trace the 1-0 numbers (0.60-0.65) to a script/CSV or remove them.
fixes.why: The claimed core 4-3 values are extrapolations; the S trend shows R43/R32 is not generally beam-independent.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Fit R43/R32 vs beam with its errors, extrapolate with the fit and uncertainty, compare with RADEX bracket.
